name: ESP32-S3 SuperMini (generic)
summary: Tiny generic ESP32-S3 board, 23.2 x 18 mm, USB-C at one end and 9 castellated pins a side.
source: There is no manufacturer and no official drawing for this board: it is a generic design sold under the same name by many sellers. The outline of 18.00 x 23.20 mm and the 20.35 mm from the first pin to the ninth come off the seller's dimensioned drawing, and the nine pins a side that implies check out exactly: eight gaps at 2.54 mm is 20.32 mm. Ten pins a side, which some listings claim, would need 22.86 mm on a 23.20 mm board and cannot be right. The pin rows are centred along the board from those two figures. What the drawing does not dimension is the gap between the two rows; it is taken to be 0.6 inch, which is what these boards use so they straddle a breadboard, and it is the one number to check with calipers before trusting a header to line up. The 1.0 mm board thickness is not dimensioned either. What is on top of the board is read off the photographs and scaled against that outline: the USB-C socket on one short edge, the boot and reset buttons either side of a small crystal, the S3 itself mounted at 45 degrees below them, and the aerial at the far end. Those are close rather than placed from a drawing, and they are decoration: no geometry is generated from them. The BAT, 48 and B+/B- pads near the USB end are extra pads rather than part of the two rows, so they are not modelled.

electrical.note: 5 V in over USB-C, 3.3 V logic. There are B+ and B- pads for a lithium cell.
